reason: Counterexample. The concave quadratic J(u) = -1/2 int |Du|^2 on H^1_0 has 0 as its only stationary point but is unbounded below; stationarity is necessary, not sufficient, and the convex sufficiency theorem does not apply. Sources [CV] Chapter 2 Section 2.4 and Chapter 5 Section 5.1, and [MA] Remark 1.5. Dependencies are the weak Euler-Lagrange theorem, the stationarity-sufficiency theorem and the in-run Poincare item. Re-recorded because the growth hypotheses and the Fatou step of [[lem-differentiation-of-an-integral-functional]] and [[thm-direct-method-for-convex-integral-functionals]] were corrected during final review (see the batch notes); this item's mathematical content is unchanged.
